I fixed the one failing check and the typecheck now passes, but there's a billing problem it doesn't catch that I left alone because it wasn't on your list.

**The fix:** in `src/adapters/openai/credit.ts:20`, the codemod had changed `usage.cachedInputTokens` to `usage.inputTokenDetails.cacheReadTokens`. That `usage` is this repo's own `ProviderUsage` type (`src/types/express.ts:19`), which still has `cachedInputTokens` and has no `inputTokenDetails`. So the codemod got it wrong, and I reverted that line to `usage.cachedInputTokens ?? 0`. `npx --no-install tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` now passes.

**The billing problem:** `src/adapters/base-adapter.ts` passes the SDK's usage object straight through as `ProviderUsage` (lines 222, 275 and 398). In v7 the SDK's usage type no longer has `cachedInputTokens`; that value now lives at `inputTokenDetails.cacheReadTokens`, according to the migration guide. TypeScript doesn't complain because every field on `ProviderUsage` is optional. But at runtime `calculateCredits` will see `cachedInputTokens` as missing, count it as 0, and bill cached input tokens at the full input price instead of the cheaper cached price.

The fix is to map `inputTokenDetails.cacheReadTokens` to `cachedInputTokens` at those three spots in `base-adapter.ts`. I can make that change if you want it.
